صفحة ٣٣٤
﴿He is worthy of piety, and worthy of forgiveness.﴾

This clause stands in the position of giving a reason (ta'lil) for the content of the clause "so whoever wills, let him remember it," reinforcing the exhortation to take heed, and taking heed leads to piety.

The meaning is: so take heed, and fear God, Exalted is He, because God is worthy of piety.

The definiteness of both parts of the clause in His saying ﴿He is worthy of piety﴾ conveys a restriction (qasr) of the one who deserves to be feared by His servants to God, Exalted is He, and that no one else deserves to be feared or to have his wrath avoided, as He said: ﴿And God has more right that you should fear Him﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37].

As for whether this restriction is a relative restriction (qasr idafi), to refute the polytheists who fear the wrath of the idols and seek their pleasure, or an assertive restriction (qasr idda'i), to specify Him, Exalted is He, with complete piety in the true sense, then, apart from this, some piety is commanded, such as piety toward the rights of kinship in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And fear God, through whom you ask of one another, and the wombs﴾ [al-Nisa': 1]. It may be said that what the Law has commanded of piety returns to piety toward God, and this is among the completions of the assertive restriction.

Ahl (أهل) of a thing means: its deserver (mustahiqquh).

Its original sense is: one who is constantly attached to a thing, its intimate, its kin, and its spouse. From this is His saying: ﴿So travel with your family﴾.

The meaning of "worthy of forgiveness" is that forgiveness is among His distinctive attributes, and that He is deserving of forgiving, by reason of His abundant mercy, the vastness of His generosity, and His beneficence. From this is the line of verse in al-Kashshaf on surah al-Mu'minun:

"Ah, have mercy upon me, O God of Muhammad;
If I am not worthy, You are worthy of it."

This is an allusive exhortation to the polytheists to give up their disbelief, on the basis that God forgives them what they have already done, as He said: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: If they desist, what has passed will be forgiven them﴾ [al-Anfal: 38]. It is also an exhortation to the disobedient to give up sins, as He said: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God. Indeed God forgives all sins. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [al-Zumar: 53].

al-Tirmidhi related from Suhayl, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said concerning this verse: "God, Exalted is He, said: I am worthy that I be feared; so whoever fears Me and does not set up with Me another god, I am worthy to forgive him." al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan gharib. Suhayl is not strong, and he alone transmitted this hadith from Thabit.

The word "ahl" is repeated in the coordinated clause, without saying "wal-maghfirah," to indicate the difference in meaning between the first ahl and the second ahl, in the manner of repeating the verb "obey" in His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, obey God and obey the Messenger﴾ [al-Nisa': 59].

صفحة ٣٣٦
In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
Surah al-Qiyamah

This surah is titled in the mushafs, in books of tafsir, and in books of Sunnah as "Surat al-Qiyamah" because the oath by the Day of Resurrection occurs at its beginning, and no oath by it was made in the surahs revealed before it.

al-Alusi said: It is also called "Surat La Uqsimu" (the surah of "I do not swear"). The author of al-Itqan did not mention it among the surahs known for having more than one name.

It is Meccan by consensus.

It is counted as the thirty-first in the order of the revelation of the surahs of the Qur'an. It was revealed after surah al-Qari'ah and before surah al-Humazah.

The number of its verses according to the counters of most of the regions is thirty-nine verses, and the people of Kufa counted it as forty.

صفحة ٣٣٧
Its purposes: It includes the affirmation of the Resurrection,
and the reminder of the Day of Resurrection and mention of its signs.

And the affirmation of recompense for the deeds that people performed in this world.

And the difference in the conditions of the people of happiness and the people of misery, and the honoring of the people of happiness.

And the reminder of death, and that it is the first stage of the Hereafter.

And the reproach against preferring the benefits of the present life over what has been prepared for the people of good of the bliss of the Hereafter.

In the tafsir of Ibn 'Atiyyah, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, though he did not attribute it with an isnad, that he said: Whoever asks about the Resurrection, or wishes to know the reality of its occurrence, let him recite this surah.

And the verses from ﴿Do not move your tongue with it﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 16] to ﴿and its recitation﴾ were incorporated into it, because they were revealed during the revelation of this surah, as will come.
